title: Ezekiel
summary: Ezekiel is a biblical book focused on exile, glory, judgment, temple vision, new heart, Spirit, and restoration.
historical_context: Ezekiel interprets exile and judgment while promising renewed presence, Spirit, and restoration.
ancient_near_east_context: Ezekiel belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Ezekiel should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Ezekiel as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Major Prophets, book 4 of 5, Ezekiel contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting exile, glory, judgment, temple vision, new heart, Spirit, and restoration to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Ezekiel as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Ezekiel uses prophecy, apocalyptic within Major Prophets, book 4 of 5 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Ezekiel helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional prophetic attribution to the named prophet
Many scholars note later collection and occasional expansion
date_ranges: 8th-6th centuries BCE with later shaping in some books
Final forms often reflect exilic or post-exilic editing
original_audience: Judah and Israel in crisis, facing judgment, exile, and restoration hopes
historical_setting: The late monarchic, exilic, and post-exilic periods
canonical_role: Ezekiel anchors exile, glory, judgment, temple vision, new heart, Spirit, and restoration within Major Prophets, book 4 of 5 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How judgment and hope are balanced

related_objects.notes: Ezekiel is the prophetic figure associated with the book.
The book is rooted in the Babylonian exile.
Temple and glory visions shape the book.
Spirit renewal is central to restoration hope.
The book promises restoration after judgment.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Ezekiel first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
